decision: authenticated replay-resistant envelope before Qubes transport binding
scope: synthetic distributed worker control plane only
winner: HMAC envelope + bounded replay cache + timestamp window

comparison.approach: HMAC envelope + replay cache + timestamp window
comparison.correctness: high for message authenticity and duplicate rejection inside one coordinator lifetime
comparison.robustness: high against tampering, stale messages, and immediate replay; secret stays outside payload
comparison.latency: very low: one SHA-256 HMAC and map lookup per message
comparison.regressionRisk: low because mission queue semantics and qrexec transport remain unchanged
comparison.qa: valid request, tampering, replay, clock skew, failed-auth retry, and bounded-memory tests

comparison.approach: trust qrexec policy alone and send unsigned JSON commands
comparison.correctness: medium because VM routing policy authenticates an endpoint but does not give the application a replay/idempotency message contract
comparison.robustness: medium-low for duplicate or stale message delivery
comparison.regressionRisk: medium because transport behavior leaks directly into mission mutation semantics
comparison.qa: would depend on Qubes-only integration tests

comparison.robustness: high and better for many independently provisioned workers
comparison.regressionRisk: medium before worker identity provisioning is stable
comparison.qa: requires key lifecycle, rotation, and revocation coverage
comparison.result: deferred until multi-Qube identity management is required

whyItWon: It separates application-level authenticity/replay fencing from the transport with minimal cost, so the same verified command contract can be carried over stdio in lab tests and qrexec later without rewriting queue behavior.
failuresAndLessons: The first test draft relied on an implicit crypto global for randomUUID; explicit import was added before CI.
The replay cache is process-local, so coordinator restart can forget seen request IDs; durable request-result reconciliation remains the next reliability gate.
HMAC does not replace qrexec policy or VM isolation; it is an application-layer defense in depth contract.
Shared symmetric secrets are acceptable for the current lab but should be revisited if workers require independent revocation or compromise containment.
nextGate: bind verified envelopes to the process coordinator request/result path, persist request IDs/results across restart, then run committed-response-loss and worker-cut fault tests before using the same adapter over real qrexec
